steps.text: Cut the lemons in half and scoop the pulp into a blender. Add half of the rinds along with sugar, vanilla extract, and 2 cups of water. Blend until smooth, then strain into a serving pitcher and stir in the remaining water.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern-Style Vanilla Lemonade
raw_recipe.description: This vanilla-scented lemonade provides a real lemon kick that's great for hot summer days! Serve over ice or frozen lemonade cubes.
raw_recipe.name: Southern-Style Vanilla Lemonade

review.reviewBody: It's my pleasure to be the first to rate this recipe. With just a hint of vanilla aftertaste, it tastes something like if Orange Julius were to make lemonade? It has just enough sweetness to bring out the vanilla flavor, but not too much to overwhelm the tartness of the lemon. Also, I'm not sure if the recipe is intended to use the entire lemon rind and not just the zest(?), as lemon pith is quite bitter. I HIGHLY recommend using Meyer lemons if you can find them. They're sweeter and much more fragrant; plus, they have minimal pith, so you can put the rinds directly into the blender without zesting!

5.20.21 My lemons may have been a bit on the small side, but with only 4 of them, I did find the flavor watered down. I added 2 additional lemons, and reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup (personal taste). One other thing, I found the vanilla totally lost in this even after doubling the quantity. Scooping out the pulp is not the easiest thing to do either, but it does help to quarter each lemon rather than halving. Also, I strained through a fine mesh strainer, and it took quite a while to drain through the blended pulp. If you’re lucky enough to have a juicer, I think you’ll find this recipe is more work, and I’m not totally convinced it’s worth it. This turned out pretty well with the adjustments I made, but I know we’d not have been satisfied made as written. Doubtful I’ll make again.

Made my own twist on this after tasting the new summer 2024 Taco Bell Vanilla Creme Limonada Freeze. Using my vitamix, a few ice cubes, 2 packets of Stevia, very generous squirt of fresh lemon juice, dash of vanilla, & some H-E-B (only in TX) lemon-lime seltzer water. It was quick & pretty darn good!!

I have a vita-mix, so I tried the recipe as is and it was too bitter. So I made another batch, with 4 lemons pealed, sugar, and vanilla. Blended this and then added the water and replaced most of the water with ice. Yum! 5 stars with my adjustments.

Husband thinks this is delicious, and I do too! I removed the peel and pith in the same manner that you peel a pineapple. This cuts out the bitterness. I added a splash of bottled lemon juice. I tripled it and added the zest of two whole lemons. I added the entire peel of half of one lemon.

This lemonade has an excellent flavor, with just a subtle hint of vanilla, though it turned out a little too bitter for my tastes. I omitted the rinds and added finely grated lemon zest instead, but next time I'll either skip this step entirely or maybe use the zest from a single lemon only, to counteract the bitterness. With that minor enhancement, I'll bet this lemonade turns into a five-star rating in my recipe box.

Pretty excited about this recipe.. Never made Lemonade before and this recipe made it soo EASY! (and Yummy!). Lemon Trees everywhere.. and all those Lemon's go to waste. Grabbed 3 HUGE Lemons from the Neighbors tree.. and WHOLA! 10 min later Super Yummy Treat. Poured some in small Glasses, added some raspberries and sliced strawberries and by the AM I'll have delicious Lemon Icy's! FABULOUS!

This lemonade is awesome as is. I've made it twice now, once as written, and the second time, I only used 1/2 C sugar. I like my lemonade a little less sweet, and a little more tart. Will definitely be a summer staple here!

I love this lemonade - it's got the perfect blend of lemon sour and vanilla musk. I use one or two more lemons than the recipe calls for because I like my lemonade nice and sour, and I largely omit the rinds to avoid the bitterness of the lemon pith. I am always grabbing 10-12 lemons at the store to stock up for this recipe!

good but not a very strong vanilla taste - i don't think i could taste it at all... and it was a lot of work... i think i'd rather just squeeze my lemons and zest them than puree the whole thing in the blender and then i could skip the step where you strain it... which was kind of messy
I added lemon juice instead of fresh lemon but still so good

Made this to go with dinner (whole roasted chicken and sage red potatoes / carrots / green beans / onion)...went perfectly with the meal. Just enough vanilla flavor but recognizable as a lemonade. Will make again. Thanks for sharing!
I love the vanilla twist. This lemonade is perfectly tart and sweet.
Delicious lemonade; reminds me a bit of muscle beach lemonade from Hot Dog on a Stick.
Very good. Got the thumbs up not only from me, but from the little ones, too.
I made this to the T..and it was okay, not the best not the worst, next time I will put more lemons... it was more like sugar water.
mmmmmm yummy! Im new to making homemade lemonade so I skipped the rind part and just blended the pulp and juice in a blender with the sugar water. I like it...the vanilla adds a great touch!
